identity.title: Holi-Spatial: Evolving Video Streams into Holistic 3D Spatial Intelligence

problem.claim: Scaling spatial intelligence requires large-scale, fine-grained 3D data.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks mainly derive QA pairs from a small set of manually annotated datasets, limiting scalability and leaving domain gaps from narrowly curated data.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Holi-Spatial, an automated pipeline for constructing a large-scale spatially aware multimodal dataset from raw videos without human intervention.
They construct Holi-Spatial-4M with multi-level geometric, object, relational, semantic, grounding, and QA supervision across 12K scenes and the reported annotation counts.
They report improved data-curation results over existing feed-forward and per-scene optimized methods, plus improved VLM performance after fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Holi-Spatial as the first fully automated, large-scale spatially aware multimodal dataset from raw video, and Holi-Spatial-4M as the first large-scale, high-quality 3D semantic dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Holi-Spatial outperforms existing feed-forward and per-scene optimized methods on ScanNet, ScanNet++, and DL3DV for data-curation quality.
The authors report substantial VLM performance improvements after fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks with the dataset.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatial intelligence is framed as dependent on abundant fine-grained 3D data.
Manually annotated, narrowly curated benchmark construction is presented as a scalability and domain-gap bottleneck.
Holi-Spatial is introduced as an automated raw-video curation pipeline with geometric and semantic supervision.
The pipeline yields Holi-Spatial-4M, combining 3DGS scenes, masks, boxes, captions, grounding instances, and spatial QA pairs.
The authors report stronger curation quality and gains from VLM fine-tuning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects the dataset’s scale to a specific inventory of supervision types and counts, then separately reports curation and downstream VLM outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: Enumerating concrete resource components before outcome claims makes the proposed data-to-capability pathway easier to assess.
lessons.application: Structure a dataset abstract by listing supervision modalities and scale, followed by benchmark comparisons and downstream adaptation results.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when the work has no concrete resource inventory or downstream evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the curation-quality metrics, numerical comparison margins, VLM baselines, or fine-tuning settings.
The reported 'first' and 'high-quality' distinctions are author claims; the abstract provides no comparative substantiation for them.
